citation: Ding F, Su CJ, Edmonds KK, Liang G, Elowitz MB. Dynamics and functional roles of splicing factor autoregulation. Cell Reports. 2022.
description: This study perturbed SRSF1 in human HEK293 cells and showed that SRSF1 uses negative autoregulatory splicing to buffer SRSF1 protein levels and adapt SRSF1 splicing activity to the demand imposed by other pre-mRNA substrates. It supports a target-specific but indirect bridge between SRSF1 dosage and RNA-processing homeostasis.

citation: Arif W, Mathur B, Saikali MF, et al. Splicing factor SRSF1 deficiency in the liver triggers NASH-like pathology and cell death. Nature Communications. 2023.
description: Acute Srsf1 deletion in mouse hepatocytes caused deleterious R-loops, DNA damage, and broad transcriptomic and proteomic disruption. It shows that SRSF1 loss can produce a global RNA/genome-integrity stress state, but in a non-neuronal tissue and without resolving the recurrent neuronal splicing-factor mRNA directions observed here.

citation: Chen H, LaFlamme CW, Wang YD, et al. Patient-derived models of UBA5-associated encephalopathy identify defects in neurodevelopment and highlight potential therapeutic avenues. Science Translational Medicine. 2025.
description: Patient-derived cortical organoids carrying pathogenic UBA5 variants showed aberrant neuronal activity, defects in GABAergic interneuron development, perturbed ER homeostasis, and exacerbated unfolded-protein-response signaling. This provides a neuronal UBA5-to-ER-stress bridge for the Uba5 rows with Ddit3/Sqstm1 or ER/mitochondrial stress components.

citation: Perdigao C, Torres J, Magnussen HM, et al. Encephalopathy-linked UFM1 variants impede neuronal protein translation, development, and function. EMBO Molecular Medicine. 2026.
description: Murine neurons with loss of the UBA5 substrate UFM1 induced ER stress, activated the unfolded protein response, reduced protein translation, and developed synaptic defects. Because it perturbs UFM1 rather than UBA5 itself, it is an indirect but pathway-specific bridge to ER-stress phenotypes after Uba5 perturbation.

citation: Serrano RJ, Oorschot V, Palipana D, et al. Genetic model of UBA5 deficiency highlights the involvement of both peripheral and central nervous systems and identifies widespread mitochondrial abnormalities. Brain Communications. 2023.
description: CRISPR uba5 mutant zebrafish reproduced neurological features of UBA5-related disease and had widespread mitochondrial damage in nervous system and skeletal muscle. It gives a target-specific bridge from UBA5 deficiency to mitochondrial pathology, although not to a directionally specified OXPHOS transcript program in mouse neurons.

citation: Liang JR, Lingeman E, Luong T, et al. A genome-wide ER-phagy screen highlights key roles of mitochondrial metabolism and ER-resident UFMylation. Cell. 2020.
description: A human CRISPRi ER-phagy screen found that ER-localized UFMylation promotes ER-phagy and restrains IRE1alpha unfolded-protein-response signaling, and that mitochondrial metabolism is required for ER-phagy. It links the UFMylation pathway to ER and mitochondrial homeostasis but is not a UBA5 neuronal loss-of-function transcriptome.
